references.text: Midian, Amalek, and the people of the East came up against Israel, describing the same enemies who gathered against Israel
The enemies came with their camels without number, like locusts in multitude - the same imagery used for the enormous enemy army
Describes the size of the Midianite army - 120,000 men fell, confirming the massive army mentioned in this verse
The comparison to sand on the seashore is a well-known biblical expression for countless multitudes, used in God's promise to Abraham
Sand on the seashore that cannot be counted - the same metaphor for an uncountable number
A great army like the sand on the seashore - identical imagery used to describe a huge enemy force
The Philistines gathered with chariots and people like the sand on the seashore - the same metaphor for an overwhelming enemy army
Locusts covered the whole land - locusts as a symbol of an overwhelming, destructive multitude
